extracted.intended_audience: Recipients of Federal education funds (K-12 and postsecondary): school administrators, Title IX coordinators, institutional counsel, and compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Federal Department of Education final-rule guidance on recipients' obligations under Title IX, including preemption of conflicting State/local law, designation and duties of Title IX Coordinators, and required nondiscrimination policies, notices, and grievance procedures. Focused on how institutions must organize, publish, and implement compliance systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preemption of conflicting State or local law (§106.6(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.6(b) clarifies that Title IX and its implementing regulations preempt any State or local law or other requirement 'that conflicts with Title IX or this part.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department maintains this preemptive effect is consistent with Spending Clause and Supremacy Clause doctrine and longstanding precedent. Preemption is limited to instances of actual conflict (e.g., impossible to comply with both or where state law stands as an obstacle to Congressional objectives). The Department removed language referencing laws providing 'greater protections' and will offer technical assistance rather than case-specific preemption opinions without investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preemption does not abrogate constitutional protections (First Amendment and Due Process)
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.6(d)(1)-(3) specifies that nothing in the Title IX regulations requires a recipient to deprive a person of rights protected by the Due Process Clauses or to restrict rights guaranteed by the First Amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final regulations should not be read to suppress protected speech; Title IX does not preempt State laws that safeguard First Amendment-protected speech. However, State laws that govern speech unprotected by the U.S. Constitution do not relieve a recipient of obligations under Title IX if they conflict with the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient remains ultimately responsible for compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient itself is responsible for compliance with obligations under Title IX, including any responsibilities assigned to the recipient's Title IX Coordinator under these final regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designating a Title IX Coordinator does not shift legal responsibility from the recipient to the individual. The recipient must ensure consistent compliance across its education program or activity and may not rely on delegation to avoid obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of a Title IX Coordinator (§106.8(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each recipient must designate a Title IX Coordinator; if a recipient has more than one Title IX Coordinator, the recipient must designate one to retain 'ultimate oversight' and 'ensure the recipient's consistent compliance' with Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final regulations permit multiple coordinators or designees but require one individual be vested with ultimate oversight. The Title IX Coordinator must be authorized to coordinate the recipient's efforts to comply with Title IX and this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of Title IX Coordinator duties (§106.8(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may delegate, or permit a Title IX Coordinator to delegate, specific duties to one or more designees (including employees or, where appropriate, independent contractors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oversight does not require a supervisory relationship; decisions about delegation are fact-specific (e.g., number of students, employees, locations) and recipients are best situated to determine when delegation is appropriate. Delegation provides flexibility to assign duties, avoid conflicts of interest, and align with administrative structure, but does not relieve the recipient of ultimate responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Title IX Coordinator contact information (§106.8(c)(1)(i)(C))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must publish the name or title, office address, email address, and telephone number of the recipient's Title IX Coordinator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nothing prevents a recipient from publicizing contact information for other designees or additional coordinators. The Department recognizes importance of community ability to identify and contact the Title IX Coordinator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt, publish, and implement nondiscrimination policies, grievance procedures, and notice of nondiscrimination (§106.8(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must adopt, publish, and implement nondiscrimination policies, grievance procedures, and notices of nondiscrimination to ensure protection from sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department added 'implement' to emphasize that mere adoption/publication is insufficient—recipients must actually follow their policies. These requirements are longstanding (since 1975). The regulations aim to make policies clear and accessible without being excessively lengthy or burdensome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for one grievance procedure consistent with §§106.45 (and 106.46 if applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department requires one grievance procedure (meaning one, or a set of, recipient procedures that are consistent with the requirements of §106.45, and if applicable §106.46) for equitable resolution of complaints of all forms of sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach ensures prompt and equitable handling while allowing flexibility for different educational environments (elementary, secondary, community college, online, research university). Additional postsecondary-specific requirements apply for sex-based harassment complaints involving a student.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of grievance procedures (who and what they cover)
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient's grievance procedures apply to complaints alleging any action prohibited by Title IX 'or' this part, and apply to complaints made by students, employees, or other individuals participating or attempting to participate in the recipient's education program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The provision is not limited to employees; 'attempting to participate' is broader than 'applying' to capture people who have applied, withdrawn, or otherwise indicate desire to re-enroll. Whether a postdoctoral trainee is an employee is fact-specific, but they may be entitled to make a complaint if participating/attempting to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of nondiscrimination content and publication (§106.8(c)(1) and (c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of nondiscrimination must notify individuals of rights protected by Title IX and how to make a report or complaint under Title IX and must be published in accordance with §106.8(c)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department favors a concise and accessible notice that adequately informs individuals how to report and how to locate the recipient's nondiscrimination policy and grievance procedures (consolidated into §106.8(c)(1)(i)(D)). The Department will not require recipients to enumerate State or local rights in the notice, though recipients may do so voluntarily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation and limits on additional notice requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declined requests to require additional items in the notice (e.g., proof of training, exhaustive lists of State/local rights, or other burdensome language).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training is required under §106.8(d) (periodic and ongoing), but requiring proof of training in the notice would create burdens (frequent updates) and is unnecessary. The Department also declines to require language stating a complainant must exhaust administrative remedies before filing with OCR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipients may retain existing policies but must modify to comply
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the final regulations precludes a recipient from retaining its existing policies and procedures but making modifications as needed to add any requirements from the final regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declines to exempt recipients from requirements based on having comprehensive existing policies; recipients must still ensure compliance with the final regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of conflict triggering preemption (e.g., laws requiring discrimination)
rubrics_metrics.description: A State law would create a conflict with the final regulations if it requires a recipient to discriminate based on a student's sexual orientation or gender identity, and such state law would be preempted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent with conflict-preemption doctrine, preemption applies when compliance with both federal and state requirements is impossible or when state law obstructs the full purposes and objectives of Congress; the Department cites earlier explanations from 2020 and Supreme Court/regulatory precedent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department technical assistance and limits on advisory opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department will offer technical assistance, as appropriate, to promote compliance with these final regulations, but will refrain from offering opinions about how the regulations apply to specific facts or specific State and local laws without first conducting an investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may seek technical assistance for compliance, but should not expect the Department to issue case-specific legal determinations outside an investigatory or enforcement context.
